evidence.for: statement I is false (AUG codes for methionine and acts as the initiator codon, not for phenylalanine)
evidence.exact_line: AUG has dual functions. It codes for Methionine (met) , and it also act as initiator codon.

evidence.for: statement I is false (phenylalanine is coded by UUU, not by AUG)
evidence.exact_line: The code is nearly universal: for example, from bacteria to human UUU would code for Phenylalanine (phe).

evidence.for: statement II (partial: one amino acid may have more than one codon)
evidence.exact_line: Some amino acids are coded by more than one codon, hence the code is degenerate.

missing: statement II is true: that AAA and AAG specifically both code for lysine
note: Statement I is shown false twice over by the salient-features list (AUG = methionine + initiator; phenylalanine = UUU), which already rules out options 1, 3 and 4 and leaves option 2. Statement II can only be half-supported: degeneracy says an amino acid may have several codons, but the AAA / AAG -> lysine assignment lives in Table 5.1, the genetic code checker-board. The passages reference that table ("Finally a checker-board for genetic code was prepared which is given in Table 5.1.") but none of them carries its contents, so no codon-to-amino-acid assignment other than UUU -> Phe and AUG -> Met is quotable here.
